newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE mission to try to reach Albania on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: OSCE mission to try to reach Albania on Thursday.

text.p: Former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky, heading a peace mission to Albania, said on Thursday he would try to reach Tirana later in the day despite reports its airport was closed.

Vranitzky, who first visited Tirana last week as head of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) mission, told a news conference he would probably travel by military plane to the Albanian capital.
Asked if he would travel by military plane, Vranitzky said: "It certainly will not be by civilian plane."

An OSCE official said the organisation was looking at ways of getting his 10-member delegation to Tirana, possibly with Italian or German military planes. International airline officials in Tirana said on Thursday the airport was closed.
Vranitzky said he did not know whether he could hold talks with insurgents who have taken control of the south of the Balkan state.

"We have had no direct reaction from anyone on behalf of the insurgents, but the message from the prime minister (Bashkim Fino) is that we may be able to have contact and might be able to organise talks," he said.
Vranitzky presented his mission's report on Wednesday to Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen of Denmark, which holds the chairmanship of the 54-member state OSCE.
"Violence by any side could spark a civil conflict of unforeseen dimension, plunging the country in a state of war," the report said.
